name: INDIAN RUMMY
description: Indian Rummy (also known as Paplu) is a popular variant of rummy played throughout India. It is a draw-and-discard game where players aim to form valid sets and sequences from 13 cards. The game requires at least two sequences, one of which must be a pure sequence (without jokers).

content.text: Indian Rummy (also known as Paplu) is a popular variant of rummy played throughout India. It is a draw-and-discard game where players aim to form valid sets and sequences from 13 cards. The game requires at least two sequences, one of which must be a pure sequence (without jokers).

Indian Rummy evolved from traditional rummy games brought to India during the British colonial period. It developed distinct characteristics and became deeply embedded in Indian culture. The game is also known as Paplu in some regions.

Minimum Players: 2
Maximum Players: 10
Optimal Players: 4-6
Partnerships: No

Type: Standard 52-card decks
Number of Decks: 2 for 2-6 players, 3 for 7+ players
Jokers: Yes (2 per deck plus one random card as wild)

2-3 standard 52-card decks
Jokers
Score sheet for tracking points

Cards per Player: 13
Dealing Pattern: Clockwise, one at a time
Wild card: One random card is turned up - all cards of this rank are wild
